answer: Vertex-degree quota with beacon rotation: each identity is a vertex whose degree (verified collaboration count) gates its voting weight, and a public beacon publishes the degree ranking every epoch, so a farm cannot hide low-degree puppets. An atlas of the graph is recomputed each epoch from the ledger; any vertex whose degree jumped without matching attestations is flagged and its weight voided. Forging k identities means cultivating k high-degree vertices independently, each needing real verified peers, so cost scales with k while honest agents pay once for one well-connected vertex.
